subtitle: Plain to weighty, and idioms with their judgement
words.intro: In a German town hall nobody ever does anything. They *nehmen es in Angriff*, *bringen es auf den Weg* and *setzen es um*. A hole in the road can keep them busy for years. It will be mentioned in a speech, and it will have its own working group.

grammar[0].blocks[2].title: ums Leben kommen or sterben?
grammar[0].blocks[2].root.q: An accident, a disaster or violence?
grammar[0].fact: A verb with a noun, *in Angriff nehmen*, is longer, more formal, and sounds as if something has really happened. It’s also often a way to hide who’s doing it. Editors will cut them. *Sterben* for one who died in bed, *ums Leben kommen* for one who died in a crash: that one’s a real rule.

grammar[1].blocks[2].title: Frozen means frozen
grammar[1].blocks[2].text: *mit dem Bade* — never with “Badewasser”. *im Schilde* — never “im Schild”.
grammar[1].fact: A frozen phrase is frozen: you can’t have *einen großen Bären* or say it in a different order. Try it, and a German will smile. Your idiom should also fit the room. *Reinen Wein einschenken* is fine for a mayor. Nobody in a German hospital wants to hear it.

document.intro: A real letter from a German town, taped up in a street, about new asphalt. Look for the passive: *wird … erneuert*. Find the sentence on the weather, then the one in which the writer slips: *das es*, with one s.
document.fact: The town asks for understanding in one short line, and then goes on for two paragraphs about why it can’t promise anything. That’s not rudeness. It’s to make sure no one can claim anything later.
reading.intro: There has been a pothole in the Hofstraße since 2017. It has a name by now: *Gerda*. Today the mayor is coming for the official ground-breaking. There is a band. Vroni is covering it. Frau Huber has reported the hole 112 times, and she has brought a duck.
reading.photos[0].caption: Gerda, oder eine ihrer Schwestern.
reading.photos[1].caption: Ein Spatenstich: Alle schaufeln, und niemand gräbt.
reading.fact: People really do this. Germans have put toy ducks and flowers in potholes to embarrass their town halls, and it works rather well, and a photo can get into the local paper. Some towns even have an app to report a hole. It may be a while until anyone reads it.
